value.body: Verifies insurance claims — health, motor or life — by visiting hospitals, sites or claimants, checking documents and collecting evidence, then reporting whether the facts match the claim. Investigation agencies working for insurers, and insurers' own claims teams, hire for this role. The day involves fieldwork and report writing.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any graduate; forensic science, life science or law backgrounds are common

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Claim files, hospital and police records, photographs, investigation report formats

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Field visits within an assigned area

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join investigation agencies or insurers' claims teams as field investigators or verification executives, usually through job portals or referrals. A two-wheeler, willingness to travel and good communication in the local language are commonly asked for.

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the work is travel and fieldwork.
Pay in agencies can be partly per case.
Experience can lead to claims, fraud-control or risk roles at insurers.
